key_insight: For a natural class of nonconvex functions, SGD with learning rate decay provably needs exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than SGD with any fixed learning rate in the small-step-size regime.
engineering_relevance: The result provides theoretical support for learning rate decay in nonconvex optimization, though it does not establish the same speedup for arbitrary engineering or deep learning objectives.
method: Analyze a nonconvex function class containing many popular benchmark functions.
Compare gradient-query complexity for decaying versus fixed learning rates.
Use weak Poincaré inequalities to prove polynomial-time annealing for the associated non-logconcave sampling task.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical exponential separation, but gives no numerical experiments or empirical performance metrics.
watch_item: The guarantee is restricted to the studied function class and small-step-size regime; practical schedule selection requires further validation.
paper_title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
